title: Introduction to AI
subtitle: Fundamentals of Artificial Intelligence
content:
🤖 What is Artificial Intelligence?

Definition: AI is the field of building systems that perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence - perception, reasoning, language, decision-making, and learning.

Important distinction: AI is the broad field. Machine Learning is one approach within AI where systems learn patterns from data. Not all AI learns from data - symbolic AI and expert systems use rules and logic instead.

Key Characteristics: Reasoning, perception, action, adaptation, language understanding.

📜 Brief History of AI

1950-1956 - Birth: Turing Test (1950), Dartmouth Conference (1956) coins the term "Artificial Intelligence."

1956-1974 - Golden Years: LISP, ELIZA, the Perceptron; optimism and heavy funding.

1974-1980 - First AI Winter: Funding cuts as early methods hit limits (Lighthill Report).

1980-1987 - Expert Systems: Rule-based systems see commercial success.

1987-1993 - Second AI Winter: Expert-system market collapses.

1993-2010 - Machine Learning Era: SVMs, statistical learning, neural networks; data and compute grow.

2010-2016 - Deep Learning Breakthrough: AlexNet (2012), GPUs, big data; CNNs dominate vision.

2016-2023 - AI Renaissance: AlphaGo, Transformers (2017), GPT/LLMs, generative AI.

2023-Present - Agentic & Multimodal AI: Tool-using agents, multimodal models, reasoning models, open-weight ecosystems.

🎯 Types of AI

By Capability: Narrow AI (current) → General AI (hypothetical) → Super AI (theoretical)

By Functionality: Reactive → Limited Memory → Theory of Mind → Self-Aware

Note: Every AI system that exists today is Narrow AI - it is specialized for a task or family of tasks. AGI remains a research goal.

💡 AI vs ML vs Deep Learning

Relationship: Deep Learning ⊂ Machine Learning ⊂ Artificial Intelligence

  • AI: Any system performing tasks that normally require human intelligence (can be rule-based or learned)
  • ML: Systems that learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed
  • DL: ML using neural networks with many layers

Quick check: A hand-written rules engine for diagnosing diseases is AI but not ML. A spam filter trained on millions of emails is both AI and ML.

🚀 Why AI Matters Now

Convergence: Data explosion + GPU/TPU acceleration + algorithm breakthroughs

Impact Areas: Productivity, Healthcare, Finance, Education, Entertainment, Science

Responsibility: With capability comes the duty to handle bias, safety, privacy, and societal impact - covered in the next lesson on AI Ethics.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Artificial Intelligence?

options.text: Systems that perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence
Systems that always learn from data
Systems that are always more accurate than humans

questions.explanation: AI is the broad field of building systems that perform tasks requiring human intelligence. Learning from data is specific to ML (a subset of AI) - symbolic AI and expert systems are AI but do not learn from data.

questions.question: A rule-based expert system for medical diagnosis is an example of:
questions.explanation: Expert systems use hand-written rules and logic - they are AI but do not learn from data, so they are not Machine Learning. ML is a subset of AI that learns from data.

questions.question: What is the relationship between AI, ML, and DL?

options.text: ML and DL are the same

questions.explanation: Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning, which is a subset of Artificial Intelligence.

questions.question: Which historical period is known as the 'AI Winter'?

options.text: 1974-1980 (and again 1987-1993) - funding cuts as early methods hit limits

questions.explanation: AI Winters (1974-80, 1987-93) followed periods of overhyped expectations; funding collapsed. They're a reminder to be skeptical of hype cycles.

questions.question: Every AI system that exists today falls into which capability category?

options.text: Narrow AI - specialized for a task or family of tasks; AGI remains a research goal
General AI - today's models can do any task a human can
Super AI - today's models exceed humans on every task
Reactive AI only - no learning whatsoever

questions.explanation: All current AI is Narrow AI (ANI). AGI (general intelligence across domains) and ASI (superintelligence) are hypothetical; no current system qualifies.
